accepted.s: Who among the following was popularly known as the ‘Lokmanya’?
accepted.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was popularly known as ‘Lokmanya’, meaning ‘beloved of the people’.
accepted.tq: Use direct identification of a leader’s popular title.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Lokmanya, Punjab Kesari, Father of Indian Unrest, Mahatma of Revolution)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Valentine Chirol used the expression ‘Father of Indian Unrest’ in his book titled:
o: The Arctic Home in the Vedas
accepted.x: Chirol used the phrase in his book Indian Unrest, published in 1910.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a famous title from the associated book title and year.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Lokmanya, Punjab Kesari, Father of Indian Unrest, Mahatma of Revolution)  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Lala Lajpat Rai — Punjab Kesari
2. Bipin Chandra Pal — Father of Revolutionary Thoughts
3. Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao — Andhra Tilak
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. Lajpat Rai was called Punjab Kesari, Pal was called the Father of Revolutionary Thoughts, and Gadicherla Harisarvottama Rao was known as Andhra Tilak.
accepted.tq: Match each leader with the exact title rather than a similar-sounding designation.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Lokmanya, Punjab Kesari, Father of Indian Unrest, Mahatma of Revolution)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremists?
accepted.x: Aurobindo Ghosh was regarded as the chief ideologue of the Extremist wing.
accepted.tq: Separate ideological leadership from organisational or moderate leadership.
accepted.sec: PERSON - Called as/Known as (Lokmanya, Punjab Kesari, Father of Indian Unrest, Mahatma of Revolution)  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following leaders was NOT associated with the Moderate group of the Indian National Congress?
accepted.x: Bipin Chandra Pal belonged to the Extremist group. R.C. Dutt, Pherozeshah Mehta and Gokhale were Moderates.
accepted.tq: Find the one leader belonging to the opposite ideological group.
accepted.sec: Moderate vs Extremist classification; regional extremist groups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following combinations is correctly matched?
accepted.x: The Maharashtra extremist group was led by Bal Gangadhar Tilak; Bengal was associated with Pal and Aurobindo, and Punjab with Lala Lajpat Rai.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure regional association and eliminate swapped leaders.
accepted.sec: Moderate vs Extremist classification; regional extremist groups  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Moderate and Extremist phases of the Congress:
1. The Moderates generally sought self-government within the British Empire.
2. The Extremists regarded British rule as exploitative.
3. The Moderates relied on self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will.
4. The Extremists drew support from students, women, workers and peasants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The three principles of self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will characterised the Extremists, not the Moderates.
accepted.tq: Identify the reversed methods statement among otherwise correct comparisons.
accepted.sec: Moderate vs Extremist classification; regional extremist groups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs correctly represents the methods associated with the Moderates and Extremists respectively?
o: Moderates—prayers, petitions and protests; Extremists—self-reliance, self-sacrifice and strong will
Moderates—boycott and mass agitation; Extremists—constitutional petitions only
Moderates—complete freedom; Extremists—self-government within the Empire
Moderates—revolutionary violence; Extremists—social reform through legislation
accepted.x: The Moderates followed the three Ps—prayers, petitions and protests—whereas the Extremists emphasised the three Ss and mass agitation.
accepted.tq: Use the paired comparison to detect reversed goals and methods.
accepted.sec: Moderate vs Extremist classification; regional extremist groups  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements correctly distinguishes the social-reform positions of the two groups?
o: The Moderates were generally pro-reform, whereas the Extremists were comparatively orthodox.
The Extremists were uniformly pro-reform, whereas the Moderates opposed social reform.
Both groups rejected all forms of social reform.
Both groups adopted identical positions on the Age of Consent Bill.
accepted.x: The Moderates were generally pro-reform, while the Extremists were comparatively orthodox; Tilak opposed the Age of Consent Bill.
accepted.tq: Test the comparison through a specific social-reform issue.
accepted.sec: Moderate vs Extremist classification; regional extremist groups  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Surat Split
B. Lucknow Pact
C. Swadeshi Movement
D. Morley-Minto Reforms
accepted.x: The sequence is Swadeshi Movement in 1905, Surat Split in 1907, Morley-Minto Reforms in 1909 and Lucknow Pact in 1916.
accepted.tq: Place the events by their years before comparing the middle items.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Swadeshi, Surat Split, Minto-Morley, Lucknow Pact, Home Rule  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Swadeshi Movement was formally launched on 7 August in which year?
accepted.x: The Swadeshi Movement was launched on 7 August 1905, following the partition of Bengal.
accepted.tq: Test the year attached to a dated movement rather than its broader phase.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Swadeshi, Surat Split, Minto-Morley, Lucknow Pact, Home Rule  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 are particularly associated with the introduction of:
accepted.x: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced separate electorates, especially for Muslims.
accepted.tq: Link a constitutional reform to its distinctive provision.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Swadeshi, Surat Split, Minto-Morley, Lucknow Pact, Home Rule  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following events took place in 1911?
o: The Partition of Bengal was annulled
The Tilak Home Rule League was founded
accepted.x: The Partition of Bengal was annulled in 1911. Tilak was released in 1914, the Lucknow Pact was concluded in 1916, and the Tilak Home Rule League began in 1916.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among closely spaced chronological milestones.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Swadeshi, Surat Split, Minto-Morley, Lucknow Pact, Home Rule  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Tilak's Home Rule League was founded on 28 April 1916.
2. Annie Besant's Home Rule League was founded in September 1916.
3. The Congress reunion and Lucknow Pact took place in December 1916.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Tilak began his league on 28 April 1916, Besant’s in September, and the reunion and Lucknow Pact occurred in December.
accepted.tq: Check dates within the same year instead of treating all Home Rule events as simultaneous.
accepted.sec: Chronology - Swadeshi, Surat Split, Minto-Morley, Lucknow Pact, Home Rule  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following newspapers was published by Bal Gangadhar Tilak in Marathi?
accepted.x: Tilak published Kesari in Marathi and Mahratta in English; both newspapers began in 1881.
accepted.tq: Distinguish paired newspapers by language and leader.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bipin Chandra Pal — The Arctic Home in the Vedas
accepted.x: Lala Lajpat Rai was associated with The Punjabee. The Arctic Home in the Vedas was written by Tilak, Unhappy India by Lajpat Rai and The Soul of India by Pal.
accepted.tq: Avoid the swapped-author trap among books and newspapers.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about extremist newspapers and writings is correct?
o: Annie Besant edited Mahratta and wrote Gita Rahasya.
Aurobindo Ghosh edited Bande Mataram and wrote New Lamps for Old.
Lajpat Rai edited Kesari and wrote Bhavani Mandir.
Tilak edited Bande Mataram and wrote Unhappy India.
accepted.x: Aurobindo Ghosh was the editor of Bande Mataram and wrote New Lamps for Old. The other options interchange the works or newspapers of different leaders.
accepted.tq: Use the author-editor association and reject swapped names.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: New Lamps for Old appeared during 1893–94 in which newspaper?
accepted.x: Aurobindo Ghosh’s New Lamps for Old appeared during 1893–94 in the Bombay newspaper Indu Prakash.
accepted.tq: Pair a work with its periodical and publication period.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who co-edited Bande Mataram with Aurobindo Ghosh according to the standard association?
accepted.x: Bipin Chandra Pal is commonly identified with Aurobindo Ghosh as a co-editor of Bande Mataram.
accepted.tq: Test the standard collaborator rather than a leader from the same movement.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following slogans is associated with Lala Lajpat Rai?
o: Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it
accepted.x: Lala Lajpat Rai is associated with the slogan ‘Go back Simon’. Tilak’s slogan was ‘Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it’.
accepted.tq: Separate slogans of closely associated Extremist leaders.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Annie Besant’s New India was originally published under which name?
accepted.x: Annie Besant’s New India was the renamed Madras Standard. She was also associated with Commonweal, begun in January 1914.
accepted.tq: Test a renamed newspaper using the original title as the key distinction.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At the Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress in 1906, which set of resolutions was passed as part of the compromise?
o: Provincial autonomy, Adult Franchise, Boycott and Home Rule
Non-cooperation, Civil Disobedience, Khilafat and Swaraj
Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education
Separate electorates, Home Rule, Dyarchy and Swadeshi
accepted.x: The 1906 Calcutta session passed resolutions on Swaraj, Swadeshi, Boycott and National Education, although Swaraj was left undefined.
accepted.tq: Recall a complete resolution set rather than one isolated item.
accepted.sec: Surat Split (1907) - president, issues, Calcutta 1906 background  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which issue at the Surat session of 1907 most clearly reflected the difference between the Extremists and Moderates?
o: Whether the Congress should support separate electorates
Whether the boycott should be extended throughout India or restricted to Bengal
Whether the Partition of Bengal should be annulled immediately
Whether the Home Rule League should be founded in 1916
accepted.x: The Extremists wanted the boycott extended throughout India, while the Moderates wanted the movement restricted to Bengal and sought to drop the 1906 resolutions.
accepted.tq: Compare the two sides on the precise disputed issue.
accepted.sec: Surat Split (1907) - president, issues, Calcutta 1906 background  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the immediate outcome of the Surat session of 1907?
o: The Extremists secured the presidency and adopted a national boycott.
The session adopted the Lucknow Pact unanimously.
The Moderates pushed the Extremists out, and the session was suspended after a scuffle.
The Congress reunited under Tilak’s leadership.
accepted.x: The Moderates, being in a majority, pushed out the Extremists; a scuffle followed and the session was suspended.
accepted.tq: Test the actual consequence rather than the causes of a famous split.
accepted.sec: Surat Split (1907) - president, issues, Calcutta 1906 background  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs correctly identifies the leadership of the two sides at Surat?
accepted.x: The Extremists at Surat were led by Tilak, while the Moderates were led by Gokhale.
accepted.tq: Avoid reversing the leaders of opposing factions.
accepted.sec: Surat Split (1907) - president, issues, Calcutta 1906 background  [other exams]

accepted.s: The Congress split at Surat was finally healed at which place and in which year?
accepted.x: The division between the Moderates and Extremists was healed at Lucknow in 1916.
accepted.tq: Link a political rupture with the later place and year of reconciliation.
accepted.sec: Surat Split (1907) - president, issues, Calcutta 1906 background  [other exams]

accepted.s: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born on:
accepted.x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak was born on 23 July 1856 at Ratnagiri.
accepted.tq: Combine the date and birthplace to defeat close-date distractors.
accepted.sec: Tilak - festivals, sedition trials, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs of public festivals and years is correctly matched with Tilak?
accepted.x: Tilak transformed Ganesh Utsav into a public festival in 1893 and Shivaji Jayanti in 1895.
accepted.tq: Keep the two similar festival dates in their correct sequence.
accepted.sec: Tilak - festivals, sedition trials, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Tilak’s educational activities:
1. He helped establish the New English School with Agarkar.
2. The Deccan Education Society founded Fergusson College.
3. The standard dates associated with these educational initiatives are 1880 and 1884.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Tilak worked with Agarkar in establishing the New English School, and the Deccan Education Society founded Fergusson College; the standard dates are 1880 and 1884.
accepted.tq: Combine institutional associations with the dates attached to them.
accepted.sec: Tilak - festivals, sedition trials, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents Tilak’s sedition-trial and imprisonment sequence?
accepted.x: Tilak received 18 months in the 1897 sedition trial, six years in Mandalay in 1908, and was acquitted in the 1916 case.
accepted.tq: Match each year with the correct legal consequence and punishment.
accepted.sec: Tilak - festivals, sedition trials, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s: Tilak was released from his imprisonment in Mandalay on:
accepted.x: Tilak was released from Mandalay prison on 16 June 1914 after his six-year imprisonment beginning in 1908.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the release date from the later Home Rule date.
accepted.sec: Tilak - festivals, sedition trials, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s: The book The Arctic Home in the Vedas was authored by:
accepted.x: The Arctic Home in the Vedas was written by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
accepted.tq: Use the author-work association while rejecting works of neighbouring leaders.
accepted.sec: Extremist leaders → newspapers, books and slogans  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Tilak’s political career is correct?
o: He joined the Indian National Congress in 1890 and founded the Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.
He joined the Congress in 1905 and founded the Home Rule League in 1914.
He joined the Congress in 1885 and founded the Home Rule League in September 1916.
He joined the Congress in 1897 and founded the Home Rule League in December 1916.
accepted.x: Tilak joined the Congress in 1890 and founded his Home Rule League on 28 April 1916.
accepted.tq: Pair two dates from the same leader’s political career and reject shifted years.
accepted.sec: Tilak - festivals, sedition trials, imprisonment, books  [other exams]

accepted.s: Who served as president of Tilak’s Home Rule League, with N.C. Kelkar serving as secretary?
accepted.x: Joseph Baptista was the president of Tilak’s Home Rule League, while N.C. Kelkar served as secretary.
accepted.tq: Distinguish office-holders within the same organisation.
accepted.sec: Tilak - festivals, sedition trials, imprisonment, books  [other exams]
